title: Chapter 12. Vasu Ghosha: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — Appearance and Childhood, Sannyasa, the Lament of Nadia, Nilachala
html:
This chapter opens the group of padas known only from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha, in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara; Gauranga's appearance on the night of the lunar eclipse, the name-giving, His first steps and "the moon from the sky"; the Lord's morning in Navadvipa and the jhulana; Vishnupriya's forebodings, the sannyasa at Katwa, the lament of Shachi and the devotees, the Lord with Advaita in Shantipura and His departure for Nilachala; the lament of Shachi and Vishnupriya; the Lord in Nilachala, His bhava of Radha, and the festival at Shrikhanda. Two padas were found in the Padakalpataru (PK) without a signature (nos. 1 and 15) — there the text follows PK; no. 27 is an abridged recension of a pada by Govinda Dasa (PK 1463). Ten padas (nos. 1, 3–5, 9–12, 14, 17) were missing from the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1 (the catalogue section on Vasu Ghosha has been supplemented). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attributing padas to Vasu Ghosha: Jagadbandhu included spurious ones as well; the childhood padas he regards as the poet's invention, and the festival at Shrikhanda (no. 29) and the pada about Svarupa (no. 28) as forgeries. The attribution of all the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional. The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2 and PK, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

1. Vasu Ghosha — "abatāra baṛa abatāra kailā baṛa…" (PK 2347; GPT1 no. 68)

Praise of the Gaura-avatara: there was no such mercy in any yuga; in every house there is the weeping of prema, the name of Hari is proclaimed; Gaura has brought a boat laden with prema to the landing and opened a market; Jagai and Madhai are saved by the name.1

অবতার বড় অবতার কৈলা বড় ।
এমন করুণা কোন যুগে নাহি কর ॥

abatāra baṛa abatāra kailā baṛa |
emana karuṇā kona yuge nāhi kara ||

abatāra — incarnation; baṛa — great; abatāra kailā — You made an incarnation; baṛa — great; emana karuṇā — such mercy; kona yuge — in any age; nāhi kara — You do not show (GPT: nāhi āra — there is no other)

1.1A great incarnation, a great incarnation You have made!
Such mercy You have shown in no other yuga.

প্রতি ঘরে ঘরে শুনি প্রেমের কান্দনা ।
কলি-যুগে হরি-নাম রহিল ঘোষণা ॥

prati ghare ghare śuni premera kāndanā |
kali-yuge hari-nāma rahila ghoṣaṇā ||

prati ghare ghare — in every house; śuni — I hear; premera kāndanā — the weeping of prema; kali-yuge — in the age of Kali; hari-nāma — the name of Hari; rahila ghoṣaṇā — remained proclaimed

1.2In every house the weeping of prema is heard;
in the age of Kali the name of Hari is proclaimed.2

সুখ-সায়রের ঘাটে দিয়া প্রেমের ভরা ।
ভাল হাট পাত্যাছ গৌর প্রেমের পসরা ॥

sukha-sāyarera ghāṭe diyā premera bharā |
bhāla hāṭa pātyācha gaura premera pasarā ||

sukha-sāyarera ghāṭe — at the landing of the ocean of happiness; diyā — bringing in; premera bharā — a boatload of prema; bhāla hāṭa — a fine market; pātyācha — You have set up; gaura — Gaura; premera pasarā — wares of prema

1.3To the landing of the ocean of happiness You have brought a boat full of prema;
a fine market You have opened, Gaura — with wares of prema!3

জগাই মাধাই তারা ছিল দুই ভাই ।
হরি-নামে উদ্ধারিলা চৈতন্য গোসাঞি ॥

jagāi mādhāi tārā chila dui bhāi |
hari-nāme uddhārilā caitanya gosāñi ||

jagāi mādhāi — Jagai and Madhai; tārā chila — they were; dui bhāi — two brothers; hari-nāme — by the name of Hari; uddhārilā — delivered; caitanya gosāñi — Chaitanya Gosani

1.4Jagai and Madhai — they were two brothers:
by the name of Hari Chaitanya Gosani saved them.4

বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে না হবে এমন ।
কলি-যুগে ধন্য নাম চৈতন্য-রতন ॥

bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe nā habe emana |
kali-yuge dhanya nāma caitanya-ratana ||

bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — Vasudeva Ghosha says; nā habe emana — there will not be such (again); kali-yuge — in the age of Kali; dhanya nāma — blessed is the name; caitanya-ratana — the jewel Chaitanya

1.5Vasudeva Ghosha says: there will be no other such;
in the age of Kali blessed is the name — the jewel Chaitanya.

no. 2451 — without a signature (in PK the pada ends at 1.4; it is preceded by PK 2346, signed by Balarama Dasa). GPT1 — pp. 46–47, no. 68 (raga yatharaga), with the closing couplet 1.5 — the signature of Vasudeva Ghosha; GPT2 — sec. 1.3, no. 68. Text of 1.1–1.4 follows PK, 1.5 follows GPT. The attribution to Vasu Ghosha is known only from GPT (a new catalogue entry, VG-154). The first line reads differently in the PK manuscripts and in GPT ("abatāra kailā baṛa baṛa" etc.), see the full version of the book. dharma of the age of Kali — CC Adi 3, 17. opens a market (hāṭa) whose "wares" are prema, given away freely. Cf. the padas about the "market" of Nityananda and Gaura (hāṭa-pattana).

2. Vasu Ghosha — "nadīyā-ākāśe āsi udila gaurāṅga-śaśī…" (GPT1 p. 51, no. 3)

The appearance of Gauranga: in the sky of Nadia the moon Gauranga has risen, and the moon of the sky, out of shame, has smeared its face with soot — the eclipse; conches and drums sound in every house; Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi are beside themselves with joy; in the darkness of the eclipse gods mingle with men, celestial women together with the women of Nadia gaze at the Child; the father gives gifts to the poor. Raga kalyana.5

নদীয়া-আকাশে আসি উদিল গৌরাঙ্গ-শশী
ভাসিল সকলে কুতূহলে ।
লাজেতে গগন-শশী মাখিল বদনে মসি
কাল পেয়ে গ্রহণের ছলে ॥

nadīyā-ākāśe āsi udila gaurāṅga-śaśī
bhāsila sakale kutūhale |
lājete gagana-śaśī mākhila badane masi
kāla peye grahaṇera chale ||

nadīyā-ākāśe — in the sky of Nadia; āsi — coming; udila — rose; gaurāṅga-śaśī — the moon Gauranga; bhāsila — floated (in joy); sakale — all; kutūhale — in delight; lājete — out of shame; gagana-śaśī — the moon of the sky; mākhila — smeared; badane — on its face; masi — soot; kāla peye — seizing the moment; grahaṇera chale — under pretext of an eclipse

2.1In the sky of Nadia a moon has risen — Gauranga,
and all are drowned in delight;
and the moon of the sky, out of shame, has smeared its face with soot,
seizing the moment — as if in an eclipse.6

বামাগণ উচ্চস্বরে জয় জয় ধ্বনি করে
ঘরে ঘরে বাজে ঘণ্টা শাঁখ ।
দামামা দগড় কাঁসি সানাই ভেঁউড় বাঁশী
তুড়ী ভেড়ী আর জয়ঢাক ॥

bāmāgaṇa uccasvare jaya jaya dhvani kare
ghare ghare bāje ghaṇṭā śām̐kha |
dāmāmā dagaṛa kām̐si sānāi bhem̐uṛa bām̐śī
tuṛī bheṛī āra jayaḍhāka ||

bāmāgaṇa — the women; uccasvare — aloud; jaya jaya dhvani kare — raise the cry "jaya, jaya"; ghare ghare — in every house; bāje — sound; ghaṇṭā — bells; śām̐kha — conches; dāmāmā — kettledrums; dagaṛa — dagar drums; kām̐si — gongs; sānāi — shehnais; bhem̐uṛa — bheur horns; bām̐śī — flutes; tuṛī bheṛī — turi and bheri trumpets; āra — and; jayaḍhāka — the great victory drum

2.2The women cry aloud: "Jaya, jaya!" —
in every house bells and conches sound;
kettledrums, drums, gongs, shehnais, horns and flutes,
turi and bheri trumpets and the great victory drum.7

মিশ্র জগন্নাথ মন মহানন্দে নিমগন
শচীর সুখের সীমা নাই ।
দেখিয়া নিমাইর মুখ ভুলিলা প্রসব-দুখ
অনিমিখে পুত্র-মুখ চাই ॥

miśra jagannātha mana mahānande nimagana
śacīra sukhera sīmā nāi |
dekhiyā nimāira mukha bhulilā prasaba-dukha
animikhe putra-mukha cāi ||

miśra jagannātha — Jagannatha Mishra; mana — (his) mind; mahānande — in great bliss; nimagana — immersed; śacīra — Shachi's; sukhera sīmā nāi — joy has no limit; dekhiyā — seeing; nimāira mukha — Nimai's face; bhulilā — she forgot; prasaba-dukha — the pains of childbirth; animikhe — unblinking; putra-mukha — at her son's face; cāi — gazing

2.3Jagannatha Mishra is immersed in great bliss,
Shachi's joy knows no bounds:
seeing Nimai's face, she has forgotten the pains of childbirth
and, unblinking, gazes at her son's face.8

গ্রহণের অন্ধকারে কেহ না চিনয়ে কারে
দেব-নরে হৈল মিশামিশি ।
নদীয়া-নাগরী সঙ্গে দেবনারী আসি রঙ্গে
হেরিছে গৌরাঙ্গ-রূপরাশি ॥

grahaṇera andhakāre keha nā cinaye kāre
deba-nare haila miśāmiśi |
nadīyā-nāgarī saṅge debanārī āsi raṅge
heriche gaurāṅga-rūparāśi ||

grahaṇera andhakāre — in the darkness of the eclipse; keha nā cinaye kāre — no one recognizes anyone; deba-nare — gods and men; haila miśāmiśi — mingled; nadīyā-nāgarī saṅge — together with the townswomen of Nadia; debanārī — celestial women; āsi raṅge — coming joyfully; herichhe — behold; gaurāṅga-rūparāśi — the whole beauty of Gauranga

2.4In the darkness of the eclipse no one recognizes anyone —
gods have mingled with men;
together with the women of Nadia, celestial women, coming joyfully,
behold the beauty of Gauranga.9

পুত্রের বদন দেখি জগন্নাথ মহাসুখী
করে দান দরিদ্র সকলে ।
ভুবন আনন্দময় গৌরবিধু সমুদয়
বাসু কহে জীব-ভাগ্যফলে ॥

putrera badana dekhi jagannātha mahāsukhī
kare dāna daridra sakale |
bhubana ānandamaya gaurabidhu samudaya
bāsu kahe jība-bhāgyaphale ||

putrera badana dekhi — seeing his son's face; jagannātha mahāsukhī — Jagannatha, overjoyed; kare dāna — gives gifts; daridra sakale — to all the poor; bhubana ānandamaya — the world is full of bliss; gaurabidhu samudaya — the rising of the moon Gaura; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; jība-bhāgyaphale — as the fruit of the good fortune of living beings

2.5Gazing at his son's face, Jagannatha, overjoyed,
gives gifts to all the poor.
The world is full of bliss — the moon Gaura has risen:
this, says Vasu, is the fruit of the good fortune of living beings.

PK, BR, KGC or PS. The preceding pada of GPT (no. 2, "jaya jaya kalaraba nadiyā nagare") is PK 1121, translated in chapter 7 (no. 6). Majumdar regards Vasu's padas on the Lord's birth and childhood as the poet's invention: Vasu was not in Navadvipa at that time (and the attribution of this pada is moreover known only from GPT). The Lord's appearance on the phalguna purnima during a lunar eclipse, when everyone was chanting the name of Hari — CC Adi 13; CB Adi 2. how the poet explains the eclipse on the night of the Lord's appearance. Shachi, like Devaki and Yashoda, only in the sweetness of love experiences it as the birth of a son (CC Adi 13; Bhag. 10.3). The words about "the pains of childbirth" convey her motherly experience in the humanlike lila. nagari-bhava. The gods who came in human guise to see the newborn Lord — CB Adi 2.

3. Vasu Ghosha — "miśra purandara kichu mane bicāriyā…" (GPT1 p. 62, no. 1)

The name-giving: Purandara Mishra calls the family priest and gives him gifts, and the priest places the arghya and his blessing on the Child's head; Shachi asks that her son be given the name "Nimai". Raga suhai.10

মিশ্র পুরন্দর কিছু মনে বিচারিয়া ।
পুরোহিত দ্বিজবরে আনিলা ডাকিয়া ॥

miśra purandara kichu mane bicāriyā |
purohita dvijabare ānilā ḍākiyā ||

miśra purandara — Purandara Mishra; kichu mane bicāriyā — having considered something in his mind; purohita dvijabare — the excellent brahmana, the family priest; ānilā ḍākiyā — called and brought

3.1Purandara Mishra, having considered something,
called to him the family priest, the best of brahmanas.

ধন রত্ন অলঙ্কার দ্বিজবরে দিল ।
স্বস্তি-বচন বলি দান তুলি নিল ॥

dhana ratna alaṅkāra dvijabare dila |
svasti-bacana bali dāna tuli nila ||

dhana ratna alaṅkāra — wealth, jewels, ornaments; dvijabare dila — he gave to the brahmana; svasti-bacana bali — pronouncing the blessing "svasti"; dāna tuli nila — (the brahmana) accepted the gift

3.2Wealth, jewels and ornaments he gave to the brahmana;
the brahmana, pronouncing his blessing, accepted the gift.

অর্ঘ্য আশীষ দ্বিজ ধরি নিজ হাতে ।
সন্তোষে তুলিয়া দিল গোরাচাঁদের মাথে ॥

arghya āśīṣa dvija dhari nija hāte |
santoṣe tuliyā dila gorācām̐dera māthe ||

arghya āśīṣa — the arghya and the blessing; dvija — the brahmana; dhari nija hāte — taking in his own hands; santoṣe — gladly; tuliyā dila — placed; gorācām̐dera māthe — on Gorachand's head

3.3The arghya and the blessing the brahmana took in his own hands
and gladly placed them on Gorachand's head.11

শচী ঠাকুরাণী কিছু কহিতে লাগিল ।
সাত পুত্রের এই পুত্র বিধি মোরে দিল ॥

śacī ṭhākurāṇī kichu kahite lāgila |
sāta putrera ei putra bidhi more dila ||

śacī ṭhākurāṇī — Shachi Thakurani; kichu kahite lāgila — began to speak; sāta putrera ei putra — this son (worth) seven sons; bidhi more dila — Providence gave me

3.4Shachi Thakurani began to speak:
"Providence has given me this son — He is to me as seven sons.12

নিমাই বলিয়া নাম দেহ দ্বিজবর ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ কহে জুড়ি দুই কর ॥

nimāi baliyā nāma deha dvijabara |
bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe juṛi dui kara ||

nimāi baliyā — as "Nimai"; nāma deha — give the name; dvijabara — O best of brahmanas; bāsudeba ghoṣa kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; juṛi dui kara — joining both palms

3.5Give Him the name 'Nimai', O best of brahmanas!" —
so, joining his palms, says Vasudeva Ghosha.

sec. 2.2, no. 1. The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; it was missing from the catalogue (new entry VG-155). On Majumdar's view of Vasu's padas on the Lord's childhood — note 5. Purandara is another name of Jagannatha Mishra. According to CB (Adi 3–4) and CC (Adi 13–14), the name "Nimai" was given to the Child by the women (born under a nim tree — as a protection), while at the name-giving ceremony the brahmanas named Him Vishvambhara; in the poem it is Shachi herself who asks for the name "Nimai". also allude to the children Shachi lost before the Lord's appearance (according to CC Adi 13 — eight daughters).

4. Vasu Ghosha — "māyera aṅguli dhari śiśu gaurahari…" (GPT1 p. 63, no. 6)

The first steps: holding His mother's finger, little Gaurahari toddles step by step, pulls her by the hand, stumbles and falls; Shachi wants to take Him in her arms, but He, being stubborn, rolls on the ground; the mother wipes Him and kisses Him. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).13

মায়ের অঙ্গুলি ধরি শিশু গৌরহরি ।
হাটি হাটি পায় পায় যায় গুড়ি গুড়ি ॥

māyera aṅguli dhari śiśu gaurahari |
hāṭi hāṭi pāya pāya yāya guṛi guṛi ||

māyera aṅguli dhari — holding his mother's finger; śiśu gaurahari — the child Gaurahari; hāṭi hāṭi pāya pāya — step by step; yāya guṛi guṛi — goes toddling

4.1Holding His mother's finger, the child Gaurahari
toddles forward step by step.

টানি লৈঞা মার হাত চলে ক্ষণে জোরে ।
পদ আধ যাইতে ঠেকাড় করি পড়ে ॥

ṭāni laiñā māra hāta cale kṣaṇe jore |
pada ādha yāite ṭhekāṛa kari paṛe ||

ṭāni laiñā — pulling; māra hāta — his mother's hand; cale kṣaṇe jore — now walks fast; pada ādha yāite — going half a step; ṭhekāṛa kari paṛe — stumbles and falls

4.2Pulling His mother by the hand, He suddenly walks faster —
and, before going half a step, stumbles and falls.

শচীমাতা কোলে লৈতে যায় ধূলি ঝারি ।
আখুটি করিয়া গোরা ভূমে দেয় গড়ি ॥

śacīmātā kole laite yāya dhūli jhāri |
ākhuṭi kariyā gorā bhūme deya gaṛi ||

śacīmātā — mother Shachi; kole laite yāya — goes to take Him in her arms; dhūli jhāri — brushing off the dust; ākhuṭi kariyā — throwing a tantrum; gorā — Gora; bhūme deya gaṛi — rolls on the ground

4.3Mother Shachi, brushing off the dust, goes to take Him in her arms —
but Gora, throwing a tantrum, rolls on the ground.

আহা আহা বলি মাতা মুছায় অঞ্চলে ।
কোলে করি চুমা দেয় বদন-কমলে ॥

āhā āhā bali mātā muchāya añcale |
kole kari cumā deya badana-kamale ||

āhā āhā bali — saying "ah, ah"; mātā muchāya añcale — the mother wipes Him with the end of her sari; kole kari — taking Him in her arms; cumā deya — kisses; badana-kamale — the lotus face

4.4Saying "ah, ah", the mother wipes Him with the end of her sari,
takes Him in her arms and kisses the lotus of His face.

বাসু কহে এ ছাবাল ধূলায় লোটাবা ।
স্নেহভরে তুমি মাগো কত ঠেকাইবা ॥

bāsu kahe e chābāla dhūlāya loṭābā |
snehabhare tumi māgo kata ṭhekāibā ||

bāsu kahe — Vasu says; e chābāla — this child; dhūlāya loṭābā — will roll in the dust; snehabhare — in the fullness of affection; tumi māgo — you, mother; kata ṭhekāibā — how much will you hold Him back

4.5Vasu says: this child will roll in the dust —
how long, mother, will you hold Him back out of tenderness?14

is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS; new catalogue entry VG-156. The neighbouring GPT padas (nos. 2–5) are PK 1141, 1161, 1150, 1151
(translated in chapter 7, nos. 8–11). On Majumdar's view — note 5.
love (vatsalya), which keeps her from seeing her Son's majesty.

5. Vasu Ghosha — "pūrṇimā-rajanī cām̐da gagane udaya…" (GPT1 pp. 63–64, no. 7)

The moon from the sky: on the night of the full moon little Nimai, seeing the moon, cries: "Give me the moon, mother!"; the moon does not come, and in despair He falls in the dust; Shachi gives Him a picture of Radha and Krishna — and He is happy: in it, says the poet, the Lord sees His own face. Raga beloar (tala dashakoshi).15

পূর্ণিমা-রজনী চাঁদ গগনে উদয় ।
চাঁদ হেরি গোরাচাঁদের হরিষ-হৃদয় ॥

pūrṇimā-rajanī cām̐da gagane udaya |
cām̐da heri gorācām̐dera hariṣa-hṛdaya ||

pūrṇimā-rajanī — the night of the full moon; cām̐da — the moon; gagane udaya — rises in the sky; cām̐da heri — seeing the moon; gorācām̐dera — Gorachand's; hariṣa-hṛdaya — heart rejoices

5.1On the night of the full moon the moon rose in the sky;
